config.title: Multi-column layout (columns)

intro.title: Multi-column layout (columns)
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple article preview with text that automatically flows into multiple columns, like in a newspaper or magazine. You will learn the core concept of the CSS `columns` property, which allows you to create multi-column layouts without needing complex grid or flexbox setups. The main technologies involved are basic CSS properties, specifically `column-count`, `column-gap`, and `column-rule`, to control the number of columns, spacing, and dividers. By the end, you'll understand how to apply these properties to structure content efficiently and responsively.
intro.usecase: Multi-column layouts are essential for organizing content efficiently in real-world applications. You'll see them used in news websites and blogs to create newspaper-like text flows, in e-commerce product listings to display items in grid formats, and in documentation pages to present code samples alongside explanations. As a developer, you'll implement columns for magazine-style articles, image galleries with consistent spacing, and dashboard widgets that need to display multiple data streams side-by-side without complex grid systems.

objectives: Apply the columns property to split text content into multiple columns
Configure column width using the column-width property
Control the number of columns with the column-count property
Manipulate the spacing between columns using column-gap
Implement column rules with column-rule-width, column-rule-style, and column-rule-color
Initialize column breaks using break-before, break-after, and break-inside
Construct a multi-column layout that spans across multiple elements

steps.title: Create the HTML structure for multi-column content
steps.instruction: Create an HTML file with a container div containing multiple paragraphs of text content
steps.hint: Start with a basic HTML structure. Add a div with a class of 'container' and inside it, add at least 3-4 paragraph elements with some text content.
steps.analogousExample:
First paragraph of text content.

Second paragraph with more content.

Third paragraph to fill the container.

Fourth paragraph for additional text.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
  <title>Multi-column Layout</title>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Add your container div with multiple paragraphs here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a complete HTML file with a container div containing multiple paragraph elements filled with text content.
successCriteria: HTML file contains a div with class 'container' and at least 3 paragraph elements inside it with text content
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a div with class 'container' and at least 3 paragraph elements inside it with actual text content.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's start with the basics. Create an HTML file with a div element that has class='container' and put several paragraph elements inside it with text content.

steps.title: Add basic container styling
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to style the container div with width: 100%, padding: 20px, and background-color: #f0f0f0.
steps.hint: Use a CSS selector for the div element and set the properties inside curly braces.
steps.seedCode:

<html>
<head>
  <title>Multi-column Layout</title>
  <style>
    /* Add your CSS rule for the container div here */
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <!-- Add your container div with multiple paragraphs here -->
</body>
</html>
steps.expectedOutcome: The container div will have a light gray background, full width, and 20px padding.
successCriteria: The CSS rule targets the div element and includes width: 100%, padding: 20px, and background-color: #f0f0f0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your CSS rule includes all three required properties: width: 100%, padding: 20px, and background-color: #f0f0f0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule is missing or incorrect. Check that you're targeting the div element and setting the required properties.

steps.title: Apply the columns property to create multiple columns
steps.instruction: Inside the existing style block, add the columns property to the container rule with a value of 3.
steps.hint: The columns property is a shorthand that sets both column-count and column-width. Use columns: 3; to create three columns.
